Vignette 1, Basic
“The Delayed Evacuation”

Scenario Background
You are the senior medical provider on site.
Location:
Offshore drilling platform

~140 miles from shore

Evacuation chain:
Nearest higher-level hospital: ~6 hours under normal conditions

Severe weather system

No air evacuation for at least 24 hours

Sea transfer unsafe

Communications:
Spotty WiFi capable of video / email / VoIP intermittently

Satellite phone

Radio capability

Teleconsult with supervising physician possible

Resources:
Limited IV fluids

Basic antibiotics

Portable ultrasound

Limited point-of-care labs (lactate, glucose, i-STAT panel)

Oxygen

No blood products

No CT imaging

Initial Presentation (Hour 0)
A 42-year-old male presents with:
2-day history of worsening leg pain

Sustained a laceration to left calf 4 days ago

Self-treated initially

Now febrile and “feels weak”

Vitals:
HR: 112

BP: 98/62

RR: 24

SpO₂: 95% RA

Temp: 39.1°C

GCS: 15

Exam:
Left calf erythematous, tense, painful

Mild purulent drainage

No crepitus

Distal pulses intact

No chest pain

No dyspnea
